h: Bacon, Giacometti and a superhero cameo
p: The heart of the centre is the collection given by Sir Robert and Lady Lisa Sainsbury in the 1970s. They had a wonderful eye for objects from very different times and places, so paintings and sculptures by modern artists such as Francis Bacon, Alberto Giacometti and Henry Moore sit alongside ancient and world art. Seeing a Bacon portrait near a centuries-old carved figure is a big part of what makes the place feel so fresh.

The building has a bit of film fame too. Its sleek, futuristic look caught the eye of Marvel, and the exterior was used as the Avengers' headquarters in Avengers: Age of Ultron. Fans of the films will get a kick out of spotting it.

The University of East Anglia campus around it is worth a stroll in its own right, with a lake, woodland paths and the stepped concrete student residences known as the ziggurats. Allow a couple of hours to see the galleries and enjoy the grounds without rushing.

Getting there is straightforward, with frequent buses from Norwich city centre to the university. Once you're back in town, Norwich Castle's Norman keep has been given an exciting new lease of life, Elm Hill is a picture-perfect cobbled lane lined with old buildings, and the colourful stripy roofs of the market are a great place to grab lunch. Norwich Cathedral, with its tall spire and peaceful cloisters, is also an easy walk from the centre.
